findings.title: MAS consultation on new retail fund types closes 10 August 2026
findings.summary: MAS published a consultation paper proposing amendments to the Code on Collective Investment Schemes (CIS Code) to enable a wider range of new fund product types to be authorised for retail offer through a streamlined process, including a new Alternative Funds Appendix. Examples include futures-based single commodity funds and single-country government bond funds.
findings.client_impact: The comment period closes today (10 August 2026). Wealth managers or clients who offer or intend to offer new Singapore retail fund types must verify whether they need to act on this consultation; failure to engage may mean missing the window to shape rules affecting their fund offerings.
findings.urgency_reason: URGENT: Consultation deadline is today, 10 August 2026. Immediate review required to determine whether a comment submission is warranted.

findings.title: Luxembourg subscription tax transition period ends 31 August 2026 — new online forms become mandatory
findings.summary: The two-year transition period for Luxembourg subscription tax filings ends 31 August 2026. From 1 September 2026, use of the new MyGuichet.lu filing forms will be mandatory for all UCIs, SIFs, and RAIFs. Identifiers (CSSF/ISIN codes) are now available for RAIF compartments, and authorities will begin systematic issuance of subscription tax account statements.
findings.client_impact: Any Luxembourg UCIs, SIFs, or RAIFs that have not yet migrated to MyGuichet.lu filing forms must do so before 1 September 2026 or face non-compliance. Fund managers and administrators have 21 days to complete the migration.
findings.urgency_reason: URGENT: Hard deadline is 31 August 2026, 21 days from today. Non-migrated funds will be out of compliance from 1 September.

findings.title: Brazil Lei Complementar 227/2026 reforms ITCMD — foreign trusts now explicitly taxable
findings.summary: Lei Complementar 227/2026 introduces progressive ITCMD (inheritance and gift tax) rates across all Brazilian states, replaces book-value with market-value assessments, and subjects foreign trusts to explicit ITCMD taxation. Brazilian-domiciled decedents' assets located abroad are now taxable by states.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian-resident HNW clients with offshore trusts, foundations, or holding structures face significantly higher ITCMD exposure, as market-value assessment and explicit trust taxation remove prior planning advantages. Existing cross-border succession plans require immediate legal review to assess restructuring options.
findings.urgency_reason: URGENT: Law is already enacted and in force. Offshore structures previously relied upon for Brazilian tax deferral are now materially less effective; clients with Brazilian residency need immediate advisory review.
findings.source_name: ZS Advogados / Multiple Brazilian law firm alerts

findings.title: CIMA AML Survey deadline for SIBA Registered Persons was 31 July 2026
findings.summary: CIMA's 2026 Anti-Money Laundering Return (AML Survey) for Securities Investment Business Act (SIBA) Registered Persons had a submission deadline of 31 July 2026. Non-compliance may constitute a criminal offence and/or result in administrative fines.
findings.client_impact: Any Cayman SIBA Registered Person that did not submit the AML Survey by 31 July 2026 is potentially in criminal non-compliance. Entities must immediately confirm whether their filing was submitted and, if not, contact CIMA and local counsel urgently.
findings.urgency_reason: URGENT: Deadline has passed. Non-compliance constitutes a potential criminal offence. Entities that have not confirmed submission must act immediately.

findings.title: Revised Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) and Transparency of Legal Entities Act (LETA) to enter into force 1 October 2026
findings.summary: The revised AMLA and LETA will enter into force on 1 October 2026. Key changes include expansion of AML obligations to 'advisors' such as lawyers advising on real estate transactions above CHF 5 million or domiciliary company formation; a new beneficial ownership transparency register for legal entities; and a codified risk-based approach requiring documented risk assessments and client categorisation.
findings.client_impact: Swiss advisors (including lawyers and fiduciaries) who assist HNW clients with real estate transactions above CHF 5 million or with Swiss entity formation will become subject to AML due diligence obligations from 1 October 2026. Clients with existing Swiss structures should review current advisory arrangements now.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Deadline is 1 October 2026, approximately 52 days away. While technically outside the 30-day URGENT window, these are the most consequential Swiss AML changes in a generation and require immediate preparation.
findings.source_name: Bollwerk AI / Multiple Swiss law firm alerts

findings.title: Panama Law 526 of 2026 introduces economic substance requirements for multinational group entities
findings.summary: Panama Law 526, enacted 28 May 2026, requires Panamanian entities that are members of multinational groups and receive foreign-source passive income (dividends, interest, royalties, capital gains) to demonstrate genuine economic substance or face a 15% flat income tax on that passive income beginning fiscal year 2027. A 90-day window for implementing regulations runs until approximately August 2026.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients using Panamanian holding or intermediate companies within international group structures to receive dividends, interest, royalties, or capital gains must assess whether genuine substance can be demonstrated or whether restructuring is warranted before fiscal year 2027 to avoid the 15% income tax.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Implementing regulations are expected imminently (90-day window runs to August 2026), and fiscal year 2027 impact requires planning now. Clients with Panama structures should engage local counsel immediately.
findings.source_name: Icaza, González-Ruiz & Alemán / Baker McKenzie / Dentons

findings.title: FinCEN proposes fundamental risk-based reform of AML/CFT program requirements
findings.summary: In April 2026, FinCEN proposed a fundamental overhaul of AML/CFT program requirements under the Bank Secrecy Act, moving from a formulaic checklist model to a risk-focused, outcome-oriented framework. A February 2026 Exceptive Relief Order (FIN-2026-R001) allows covered financial institutions to apply a more risk-based approach to beneficial ownership verification at new account opening.
findings.client_impact: US financial institutions in FGC's network may update their AML/KYC onboarding procedures under the new risk-based framework, which could affect account opening documentation requirements for HNW clients. The proposed reform, if finalised, would significantly reshape compliance obligations across US-regulated counterparties.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: The April 2026 proposal is under review; the February 2026 Exceptive Relief Order is already operative. Final rules not yet issued but signal a directional shift in US AML/CFT compliance.

findings.title: OECD Pillar Two Side-by-Side Package released — four new safe harbors, Qatar activates registration August 2026
findings.summary: In January 2026, the OECD released its Pillar Two 'side-by-side package' incorporating new Administrative Guidance into the Model Rules, including four new safe harbors. GloBE Information Return (GIR) first filings for calendar-year taxpayers were due 30 June 2026. On 2 August 2026, Qatar activated its Global and Domestic Minimum Tax registration service. Approximately 140 countries have now adopted Pillar Two.
findings.client_impact: Multinational groups with HNW beneficial owners operating in Pillar Two-implementing jurisdictions must ensure GIR filings are completed and take advantage of newly available safe harbors to minimise top-up tax exposure. Qatar registration is an immediate compliance step for entities with Gulf operations.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: The GIR June 2026 filing deadline has passed; entities should confirm compliance. Qatar and other new jurisdictions continue to activate registration, requiring ongoing attention.

findings.title: BVI beneficial ownership regime fully operational since 1 April 2026 — legitimate interest access now available
findings.summary: As of 1 April 2026, persons able to demonstrate a qualifying legitimate interest may apply for access to limited beneficial ownership information concerning BVI UBOs with 25%+ ownership or control. The moratorium on penalties for late filings ended 31 March 2026. Entities must file UBO information within 30 days of incorporation or any subsequent change.
findings.client_impact: Clients with BVI entities must ensure their UBO information is currently filed and accurate, as the penalty moratorium has ended; any changes in beneficial ownership now trigger a 30-day filing obligation and late filings are subject to enforcement.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Regime is fully live; moratorium ended April 2026. Ongoing compliance obligation — any outstanding or future UBO changes require timely filing.

findings.title: Luxembourg new carried interest tax regime for AIF managers applies from 2026 tax year
findings.summary: Luxembourg introduced a new tax regime for carried interest granted to managers of alternative investment funds (AIFs), applying from the 2026 tax year. The regime modernises Luxembourg's carried interest rules and requires fund managers and sponsors to review LPAs and waterfall provisions for alignment.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients who are Luxembourg AIF managers or investors in Luxembourg AIFs with carried interest structures should review their limited partnership agreements and waterfall arrangements to ensure alignment with the new regime before year-end 2026.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Applies from the 2026 tax year (now current). LPA reviews and potential restructuring should be completed before year-end.

findings.title: India CBDT revises FATCA/CRS guidance — digital assets now in scope for CRS reporting; CRS form deadline September 15, 2026
findings.summary: On 24 July 2026, India's CBDT released revised guidance on FATCA and CRS compliance, bringing digital assets (e-money wallets, CBDC holdings, crypto derivatives, stablecoin accounts) into the CRS reporting framework. Entity classification rules were tightened. The CRS Compliance Form deadline is September 15, 2026.
findings.client_impact: Wealth managers and financial institutions with India-reportable accounts holding digital assets must ensure their CRS reporting systems capture the new asset categories. HNW clients with Indian tax residency or Indian-connected accounts may face expanded reporting obligations for digital asset holdings.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: CRS Compliance Form deadline is September 15, 2026 (36 days away). Reporting systems and entity classifications should be updated immediately to capture digital assets.

findings.title: EU AMLA now operational in Frankfurt; AMLR applies from July 2027 — RTSs in development
findings.summary: The EU's Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) is now operational. AMLA is drafting 13 regulatory technical standards (RTS) and 6 implementing technical standards (ITS), with drafts expected mid-2026. The Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR) will apply from 10 July 2027, replacing the directive-based approach. From 1 January 2028, AMLA will directly supervise 40 large high-risk financial institutions.
findings.client_impact: EU-based wealth management entities in Luxembourg, Malta, Cyprus, and other member states must begin AMLR readiness assessments now; the regulation introduces uniform EU-wide obligations that may significantly exceed current national AML requirements, and AMLA's draft RTSs will define key operational details.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: AMLR applies July 2027 — approximately 11 months away. Preparation should begin now, particularly as RTSs (mid-2026 drafts) define key compliance parameters.
findings.source_name: AMLA / KPMG / Norton Rose Fulbright / DLA Piper

findings.title: Cyprus establishes National Sanctions Implementation Unit and prepares for EU AMLA RTS requirements
findings.summary: Cyprus has established a National Sanctions Implementation Unit (NSIU) to centralise sanctions enforcement across the financial sector. Cyprus-regulated entities (CIFs, AIFMs, UCITS managers, CASPs, RAIFs) are preparing for EU AMLA Regulation requirements. A 2025 amendment brings crypto asset service providers under the 'financial institutions' definition.
findings.client_impact: Cyprus-domiciled investment structures and their managers face new sanctions screening obligations through the NSIU and must begin planning for EU AMLA compliance. Clients using Cyprus vehicles (RAIFs, CIFs) should confirm their administrators are updating AML/sanctions policies.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: AMLA RTS drafts expected mid-2026; NSIU already operational. Ongoing monitoring of Cyprus regulatory output is required through 2027.

findings.title: Central Bank of The Bahamas published revised AML/CFT/CPF guidance — enhanced enforcement provisions
findings.summary: The Central Bank of The Bahamas revised its AML/CFT/CPF Guidelines (last revised 19 March 2026) and published an updated Guide to the AML/CFT/CPF Ladder of Supervisory Intervention. Key changes include requirements for annual follow-up risk assessments, mandatory appointment of compliance officers and MLROs, and strengthened enforcement including penalties up to BSD 100,000 per contravention.
findings.client_impact: Bahamas-based entities in FGC's network (banks, trust companies, securities firms) must ensure their AML programmes are updated to meet the revised 2026 standards including annual risk assessments and mandatory MLRO appointments, or face significantly higher penalties.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Guidelines already in force since March 2026. Entities should confirm their programmes are updated and annual risk assessments are scheduled.

findings.title: MFSA launches Financial Crime Compliance Strategy 2026
findings.summary: The MFSA published its Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) Strategy 2026, a risk-based and outcomes-driven supervisory model to combat financial crime across the financial services sector. The strategy adopts a lifecycle approach to oversight covering authorisation, supervision, and enforcement, and aligns Malta with evolving EU AML/CFT requirements. Higher-risk sectors will receive directed supervisory resources.
findings.client_impact: Malta-regulated entities involved in wealth management and fund administration should expect increased MFSA AML supervisory scrutiny, particularly in higher-risk business lines; enhanced due diligence and documented risk frameworks will be prioritised in supervisory reviews.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Strategy is operational now and will shape MFSA enforcement priorities through 2026. Malta-regulated entities should review their compliance posture against the FCC Strategy.

findings.title: Isle of Man Verification of Entity Registration Bill 2026 passes Tynwald, awaiting Royal Assent
findings.summary: The Verification of Entity Registration Bill 2026 completed its passage through Tynwald in July 2026. It introduces measures to support registration, verification, and oversight of legal entities, ensuring beneficial ownership information on IoM registers is accurate and up to date. It forms part of a broader FATF compliance programme and is now pending Royal Assent.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Isle of Man entities (companies, partnerships) should anticipate enhanced registry transparency requirements and potential reverification of beneficial ownership information once the Bill receives Royal Assent and implementing guidance is issued.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Royal Assent and commencement date not yet confirmed. Clients with IoM structures should monitor for implementing regulations and be prepared for a UBO reverification process.
findings.source_name: Isle of Man Financial Services Authority (IOMFSA)

findings.title: Brazil BCB VASP authorisation deadline is 30 October 2026 — VASPs must apply now
findings.summary: Virtual Asset Service Provider regulations came into force in Brazil on 2 February 2026. VASPs already operating in Brazil must formally apply for BCB authorisation by 30 October 2026 or cease operations. The BCB is the central VASP regulator; the CVM has jurisdiction where crypto-assets qualify as securities.
findings.client_impact: Wealth managers with clients who hold crypto-assets through Brazilian VASPs should verify that those VASPs have applied for BCB authorisation; unregistered VASPs must cease operations after 30 October 2026, creating asset custody risk for any client assets held on non-compliant platforms.
findings.urgency_reason: WATCH: Deadline is 30 October 2026 (81 days away). Verification of counterparty VASP authorisation status should be completed in the near term to protect client assets.

findings.title: MFSA publishes administrative penalties methodology for credit institutions
findings.summary: The Malta Financial Services Authority (MFSA) published a new Guidance Note outlining its methodology for determining administrative penalties on credit institutions for regulatory breaches, establishing transparent, structured, proportionate, and dissuasive enforcement measures aligned with EU AML/CFT requirements.
findings.client_impact: While directed at Malta credit institutions rather than wealth managers directly, this framework signals MFSA's increased enforcement focus and provides transparency on penalty calibration relevant to assessing Malta-based banking and custody counterparty risk.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Directed at credit institutions, not wealth managers. Relevant as background on Malta's AML enforcement environment and counterparty risk assessment.

findings.title: JFSC launches Jersey IP register and myIPO online service; streamlines foreign company continuation
findings.summary: In July 2026, the JFSC launched Jersey's intellectual property register and myIPO online service ahead of new legislation taking effect 1 August 2026. The JFSC also announced a streamlined application process for foreign companies continuing into Jersey, with a single form, one payment, and clearer guidance, reducing friction for structures re-domiciling to Jersey.
findings.client_impact: Clients considering re-domiciling corporate structures to Jersey will benefit from a simpler continuation process effective August 2026; this may make Jersey more attractive as an alternative to BVI or Cayman for international holding structures.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Procedural improvement already in effect. No action required but useful context when advising on Jersey re-domiciliation as a structuring option.

findings.title: Guernsey registers first fund under Sustainable Funds Regime covering two designations
findings.summary: In June 2026, the Guernsey Financial Services Commission (GFSC) registered the first island fund to qualify under two parts of Guernsey's Sustainable Funds Regime, combining the Green Fund and Natural Capital Fund designations. Guernsey also won the Sustainability Programme category at the Wealth for Good Awards 2026.
findings.client_impact: Clients interested in ESG or impact investment vehicles now have a precedent for dual-designation sustainable fund structures in Guernsey, which may appeal to philanthropically oriented HNW families or family offices seeking demonstrable ESG credentials for their investment vehicles.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: A positive market development for ESG fund structures in Guernsey. No compliance action required; informational for wealth managers advising on sustainable investment.

findings.title: US formally not implementing OECD Pillar Two — Treasury exempts US-headquartered companies
findings.summary: In January 2026, the US Treasury announced that US-headquartered companies are exempt from Pillar Two's global minimum tax requirements, and the United States will not be implementing Pillar Two. US-based multinational groups with subsidiaries in Pillar Two-implementing jurisdictions may still face top-up taxes in those local jurisdictions.
findings.client_impact: US-domiciled HNW families with operating businesses or investment holdings through foreign subsidiaries in Pillar Two countries need to assess whether those subsidiaries face top-up taxes under local QDMTT or IIR rules, even though the US federal government is not imposing Pillar Two.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Decision was made in January 2026. No new immediate action required, but ongoing planning consideration for US clients with multinational group structures in Pillar Two jurisdictions.

findings.title: CIMA increases Fund Annual Return (FAR) filing fee by ~28% effective January 2026
findings.summary: CIMA increased the Fund Annual Return (FAR) filing fee by approximately 28% effective January 1, 2026, rising from CI$350 (~US$427) to CI$450 (~US$549) per fund annually. This affects all Mutual Funds and Private Funds registered with CIMA.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Cayman-registered funds face increased annual compliance costs of approximately US$122 per fund per year; administrators and fund managers should update their fee budgets accordingly for 2026 and subsequent years.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Fee increase already in effect since January 2026. Informational for cost budgeting purposes.

findings.title: UAE Capital Market Authority (CMA) new federal framework in force since January 2026
findings.summary: On January 1, 2026, UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 32/2025 (CMA Law) reconstituted the SCA as the Capital Market Authority (CMA) with broader supervisory and enforcement powers, and Federal Decree-Law No. 33/2025 introduced a statutory prospectus liability framework, safe harbors for price stabilisation, and explicit application to foreign issuers including DIFC/ADGM-incorporated entities offering or trading securities in the UAE.
findings.client_impact: Clients with investment structures incorporated in DIFC or ADGM that offer or trade securities in the UAE must review compliance with the new prospectus liability rules; the CMA's broader supervisory powers signal more active UAE securities enforcement going forward.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Framework already in force since January 2026. No immediate deadline, but relevant context when advising on UAE-connected securities offerings or DIFC/ADGM structures.

findings.title: Florida SB 264 foreign buyer restrictions upheld; 2026 proposed expansion failed to pass
findings.summary: Florida's SB 264, restricting real estate purchases by nationals of designated 'countries of concern' (China near-total ban; Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela, Syria restricted near military/critical infrastructure), was upheld by the Eleventh Circuit in November 2025. A 2026 proposed expansion to additional residential categories failed to pass. Standard FIRPTA withholding for foreign sellers remains at 15% of gross sales price.
findings.client_impact: Foreign national clients from the designated countries of concern remain subject to SB 264 restrictions on Florida real estate near military or critical infrastructure. No new restrictions were added in 2026; FIRPTA at 15% continues to apply to all foreign sellers of US real property.
findings.urgency_reason: FYI: Status quo maintained. No change from prior position; informational for clients subject to SB 264 restrictions or transacting in Florida real estate as foreign sellers.
findings.source_name: Akerman LLP / South Florida Law / Finberg Firm
